title: SMART Trust demonstrator architecture
description: The people, systems, parts, journeys and per-country building blocks the demonstrator's ArchiMate overlay on the DPI-H RA draws, one concept each; each model element names its concept by skosConcept. Generated by tools/ig-gen/ig_gen.py.

terms.definition: The parent who holds the child's paper DVCs and the family phone, and presents them; IHE ITI VHL VHL Holder and smart-trust Holder.
The clinician abroad who gives the birth doses and hands over the signed paper DVC (J1).
Finds unregistered children on home visits, registers them and refers them to the clinic (J2).
The nurse at the home clinic who receives the referral, has the foreign DVCs verified and decides catch-up doses (J3).
The clinician abroad who scans the family's QR and reads the child's records (J4.1).

terms.prefLabel: Chiang Rai primary care clinic viewer, Thailand (J4.1)
terms.definition: The VHL viewer of a primary care clinic in Chiang Rai, Thailand, back in Country A a year after the birth (J4.1): verifies the VHL, fetches the manifest with an HTTP Message Signature after the passcode is entered, and decrypts the documents for viewing. Its trust store is loaded before the visit from a cache of the GDHCN trust list refreshed nightly or hourly; verifying needs no connection.

Reads a Verifiable Health Link QR at the point of care, checks its signature against the GDHCN trust list, fetches the manifest from Lao PDR with a signed request and shows the decrypted records (J4.1).

terms.prefLabel: Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital system, Thailand (Country A, XXR)
terms.definition: The hospital record system and DVC issuing service of Chiang Rai Provincial Hospital in Thailand (Country A, the birth country): issues one DVC per birth dose (J1), signing with the DSC of GDHCN DEV test participant XXR (kid kW/6VnwPRKI=, hex 916ffa567c0f44a2), which plays Thailand in the demonstrator. XXR is a DEV test participant, not Thailand's production key.
The hospital's electronic health record, in which the vaccinator records each birth dose given to the newborn (J1).
Keeps the newborn's immunizations as FHIR Immunization resources, from which each DVC is made (J1).
Publishes the vaccine product codes the hospital records doses against, which the receiving country maps to its own schedule codes (J1, J3).
Builds each Digital Vaccination Certificate as an HCERT payload and has it signed with Thailand's document signer key, published to GDHCN (J1).

The OHS app on the community health worker's phone in Lao PDR (J2), community configuration, offline: adds the newborn to the household (structured data capture), triage-reads a foreign DVC without verifying it (STT-VER-011), saves the doses as reported, not verified, and records a referral. A Receiver that deliberately stops before trust.
The registration and referral forms of the CHW app, FHIR Questionnaires filled in with Structured Data Capture, which also read the doses on a paper DVC (J2).

terms.prefLabel: Vientiane District Health Center EHR (Country B)
terms.definition: The district health center's OHS-based record system in Lao PDR (Country B), on a tablet (J3): verifies DVCs against its cached GDHCN trust list, imports them with provenance, adds the Lao schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code and evaluates the national schedule. A Receiver; Country B, as a Trust Network Participant, retrieves the PKI material it uses. Its trust store is loaded before the visit, from the copy of the trust list it refreshed when last connected (for an offline clinic, about weekly); it fetches nothing during J3.
The health centre's record of each patient, where imported immunizations are kept with their provenance (J3).

terms.prefLabel: Code mapping service (product to Lao EPI)
terms.definition: Maps a foreign vaccine product code to the Lao EPI schedule code, which is added beside the original code on import (J3).
Evaluates the Lao infant immunization schedule against the child's doses, imported ones included, and says which are due (J3).
Verifies a DVC's HCERT signature against the GDHCN trust list cached on the device (J3).

The one Android phone the Sengmany family shares, held by Bounmy (J4): a family wallet with a profile per member (Bounmy, Khamla, Somsack) and one VHL QR per member, presented by the VHL Holder. It is the Holder's device, not an actor of its own in either guide.
The wallet app on the family's phone: a profile per family member, each holding that member's VHL QR, shown when asked (J4.0, J4.1).

WHO's Global Digital Health Certification Network, DEV environment: receives participants' PKI material and distributes it as DID trust lists (DEV: tng-cdn-dev.who.int). Country A (Thailand, played by XXR) and Country B (Lao PDR, played by the fictional XXH) are its participants.

terms.prefLabel: Lao PDR national health portal and gateway (Country B, XXH)
terms.definition: Lao PDR's national FHIR server behind the OHS FHIR Info Gateway (J4.0, J4.1): assembles each family member's IPS and DVCs, issues each as a passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link in an HCERT signed with Country B's DSC, hosts the manifests (ITI-YY5), checks passcode, expiry and consent on each request, and logs every access as an AuditEvent at home. Country B is played on the GDHCN DEV network by the fictional participant XXH, so no real ministry's key is implied.
Holds each person's records (IPS, DVCs) as FHIR resources, from which the portal assembles what a VHL shares (J4.0, J4.1).
Issues a passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per family member, in an HCERT signed with Lao PDR's document signer key (J4.0).
Answers a VHL manifest request after checking its signature, the passcode, the expiry and the consent, and logs each access in Lao PDR (J4.1).
Identifies each person the portal serves, children and their households included.
Lists the clinics and health centres that record and share care.
Lists the health workers, community health workers and nurses among them, who record care.
Copies the portal's FHIR data into an analytics store for reporting.

terms.prefLabel: XXR document signer key (Country A, Thailand)
terms.definition: The private key of XXR's document signer certificate (DSC), kid kW/6VnwPRKI= (hex 916ffa567c0f44a2), whose public DID document is on the GDHCN DEV trust list (did:web:tng-cdn-dev.who.int:v2:trustlist:-:XXR:DSC, as the DEV host serves it; the guide prints the production host, smart-trust-tools OI-34). XXR is a Trust Network Participant.

terms.prefLabel: J1 Issue the newborn's birth-dose DVCs in Country A
terms.definition: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives a newborn who is not its own country's national the Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the WHO guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example is such a pair). The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL).

terms.prefLabel: J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B
terms.definition: J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXH), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, through a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, STT-VER-011: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs when it next has a signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver).

terms.prefLabel: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic
terms.definition: J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them.

terms.prefLabel: J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs
terms.definition: J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who holds the family's one shared phone asks Country B's national portal for each family member's records, choosing for each a passcode the family can say aloud and an expiry (for example 14 days); the portal records that choice as the holder's consent to share (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, a VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per member: the documents (IPS, DVCs) encrypted as JWE (STT-VHL-007) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR carries only a pointer and a key.

terms.prefLabel: J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad
terms.definition: J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly.
